claude_proposed_widenings.name: resource_pool family for class features
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Font of Magic's primary mechanic is establishing a named, level-scaled spendable point pool (Sorcery Points). The existing 'activation' family models a one-shot feature that consumes a use_count and produces a single ClassFeatureEffect. A bidirectional currency pool with partial spending, multi-operation support, and external refill (from spell slots) requires a distinct family.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: You have 2 Sorcery Points, and you gain more as you reach higher levels, as shown in the Sorcery Points column of the Sorcerer Features table. You can't have more Sorcery Points than the number shown in the table for your level. You regain all expended Sorcery Points when you finish a Long Rest.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: resource_conversion ClassFeatureEffect variant
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Two distinct conversions are needed: (1) expend a spell slot of level N to gain N Sorcery Points (no action), and (2) expend SP per a cost table to create a temporary spell slot (Bonus Action). Neither operation maps to GrantExtraActionEffect or HealHpEffect. A new 'resource_conversion' shape must model: source resource type, drain amount (fixed or table-keyed), target resource type, gain amount, activation cost, and optional expiry condition on the created resource.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: Converting Spell Slots to Sorcery Points. You can expend a spell slot to gain a number of Sorcery Points equal to the slot's level (no action required). Creating Spell Slots. As a Bonus Action, you can transform unexpended Sorcery Points into one spell slot. [...] Any spell slot you create with this feature vanishes when you finish a Long Rest.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: point_pool UseCountResource variant (or parallel type)
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: UseCountResource with ThresholdTiers<number> cap is structurally close but semantically wrong. A use_count is discrete (used / not used). Sorcery Points are a fractionally-spendable pool whose current value can range from 0 to max in any increment, and can be partially refilled mid-session (by converting spell slots). Conflating these would produce a misleading trace. A new 'point_pool' type with a named pool identifier, a per-level-cap schedule, and a partial-spend semantic is needed.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: You have 2 Sorcery Points, and you gain more as you reach higher levels [...] You can use your Sorcery Points to fuel the options below, along with other features, such as Metamagic, that use those points.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: long_rest_expiry lifecycle atom or Duration variant for created resources
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The spell slot created by the SP→Slot operation carries an expiry condition ('vanishes when you finish a Long Rest') that is distinct from the slot's normal lifetime. No existing Duration, lifecycle atom, or effect shape represents 'this resource instance was created temporarily and expires on the next long rest regardless of use'.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: Any spell slot you create with this feature vanishes when you finish a Long Rest.
